rows.description: My father says he also felt lost in a new place as a child. Hearing that makes me feel less alone. Sharing feelings with parents helps, and small routines like a weekend outing settle me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, grief, loneliness, mockery, resentment, trust

rows.description: My grandfather is in the hospital and I am afraid he may die. Fear like this is natural. I ask an adult honest questions and draw or pray or sit with him. Not being told anything is scarier.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, compassion, grief, guilt, protectiveness

rows.description: I sit near my grandmother and read to her while she rests. Small caring acts matter to sick people. I do not have to fix anything; being present is enough.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, fear, grief, guilt, protectiveness

rows.description: My parents whisper and hide the truth about grandpa. I feel more scared not knowing. Wise parents share simple honest information and let a child visit or help. Hiding it does not protect me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, compassion, fear, grief, guilt

rows.description: I remember that I was rude to my grandmother before she got sick and now I feel guilty. I can tell her sorry and I love you now. Guilt shows love, and I do not have to carry it forever.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, compassion, fear, grief, protectiveness

rows.description: My grandfather has died and I feel empty, angry and confused. All of those are grief. I can cry, ask questions, share memories and take part in the rituals if my family does. Grief comes in waves.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, compassion, fear, guilt, protectiveness
related mind states: sadness, grief, anger, confusion

rows.description: My mother is crying because her father is ill and I feel helpless. I can hug her and stay near. I do not have to fix her feelings. Seeing that grown-ups cry too teaches me it is okay.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, compassion, fear, guilt, protectiveness
related mind states: affection, sadness, grief

rows.description: My friend's grandmother is ill and she is quiet. I sit with her, share my snack and do not ask too much. Being a kind presence is enough. Saying it will be fine may not help her.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, fear, grief, guilt, protectiveness

rows.description: The doctors are helping my grandfather and I try to trust them. I can ask my parents what they are doing in simple words. Understanding a little cuts down my fear. I also prepare for uncertainty.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger, compassion, fear, grief, guilt

rows.description: My sister and I snap at each other because we are both scared. Stress comes out as anger. Wise: notice it, apologise, and comfort each other. Fighting when frightened is common but we can choose kindness.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, compassion, fear, grief, guilt, protectiveness
